title: Wilmot land assembly report deferred pending legal opinion
subtitle: Also: supervised-consumption advocacy, Solve the Crisis campaign, Kissing Bridge Trailway bridge, expropriations for two roundabouts, ambulance response targets.
overview: Council spent most of the evening on the staff report about the removal of a premature corn crop on the Wilmot land assembly site. Several delegates, including a farm federation representative, called the report incomplete and asked for an apology and an end to the assembly. Staff said confidentiality obligations limited what could be said in open session. Council deferred the matter to October 23, 2024, pending a legal opinion on whether the non-disclosure agreement and other confidentiality agreements remain valid {{vote:m3}}.

Council also approved the 2025 ambulance response time plan, along with a resolution urging Ontario to keep funding consumption and treatment sites {{vote:m7}}. It backed the Solve the Crisis campaign on homelessness, mental health and addictions {{vote:m12}}. Expropriation of land for roundabouts at Fischer Hallman and New Dundee roads and at Roseville and Edworthy Side roads was approved {{vote:m8}}. Up to $150,000 was set aside for public art at the Langs Drive redevelopment {{vote:m6}}.

Council also approved $250,000 more for Franklin Boulevard design and construction work {{vote:m9}}. A report on a Conestogo River pedestrian bridge on the Kissing Bridge Trailway is due November 5. Staff reported a current estimate of $8 million, with the Region's share depending on grant and partner funding.

decisions.detail: Council deferred the report and a motion seeking more detail to October 23, 2024, pending a legal opinion on whether the non-disclosure and other confidentiality agreements are valid.

decisions.item: Ambulance response times and drug-site advocacy
decisions.detail: Council approved the 2025 Response Time Performance Plan and urged Ontario to keep funding consumption and treatment sites and HART hubs beyond March 2025.

Council approved expropriating land for roundabouts at Fischer Hallman/New Dundee and Roseville/Edworthy Side roads, and directed staff to prioritize analysis of a Conestogo River trail bridge and apply for provincial funding.
Council supported the campaign and called on the provincial and federal governments to act on homelessness, mental health and addictions, including a responsible provincial minister and a task force.
Council approved up to $150,000 from the Public Art Reserve for permanent artwork at the Langs Drive redevelopment in Cambridge.
Council added $250,000 to the Franklin Boulevard capital project from the Transportation Capital Reserve.

debate: Delegates said the report did not explain who removed the crop or why. They said it left out the costs, and that farm groups were not consulted. They asked for the assembly to be taken off the table and said farmers were unwilling hosts.

Staff said confidentiality obligations to landowners and other parties limited what could be shared in open session. They offered to discuss more in closed session and said naming the feed producers or biofuel company contacted could expose them to harassment.

One councillor argued the non-disclosure agreement no longer applies because provincial ministers had spoken publicly about it. Others said staff had advised it remains in effect and that Council should not assume otherwise. The disagreement led to the legal-opinion deferral.
Some councillors said Council had not been told about the crop removal in advance. Others said elected members, not staff, are accountable and that staff should not take the blame.

On the Kissing Bridge Trailway, staff said provincial landlord approval was still needed. They said the Region's share could range from about $500,000 to $4 million depending on grant and partner funding, and that a project manager would be needed.
